messages:
maria: quick pulse check 

I prototyped a "batch demote manifest" to mitigate the traffic surge we see during tenant drains. posting the gist + a few operational ideas before i put together an RFC.

kevin: curious 

how is this different from a plain broadcast?

maria: instead of N per-prefix RPCs, we send 1 compressed manifest per target node. manifest contains list of prefix ops + expected_version + idempotency token. nodes apply locally with CAS semantics. reduces RPC QPS and lets us retry selectively.

sam: sounds promising. failure semantics? partial apply scares me for reads.

maria: plan: each entry CASes against expected_version. node reports applied vs failed. coordinator keeps per-manifest state and can retry failed entries. readpath checks pending_manifest_set to avoid stale returns.

anita: ops implications? will this hide failures? need pause/abort and visibility in console.

maria: yes 
we add manifest status (pending/partial/succeeded/aborted) + per-node ack list. UI: manifest view with per-prefix results and retry/abort actions. canary flag to apply to subset of nodes first.

kevin: minimal example?

maria: pasted quick shape below 

```json
{
  "manifest_id": "m-1769919999-a",
  "epoch": 2048,
  "entries": [
    {"prefix": "acct/900/pfx1", "op": "demote", "expected_version": 17, "token": "tok-1"},
    {"prefix": "acct/900/pfx2", "op": "evict",  "expected_version": 3,  "token": "tok-2"}
  ],
  "sample_nodes": 10
}
```

sam: good. what about ownership/lease boundaries? manifests should be accepted only if node currently owns prefix epoch.

maria: exactly. apply gated by ownership check. entries can include expected_owner_epoch to be extra-safe.

ryan: for testing i'll add a simulation that injects partial network failures, mid-manifest crashes, and conflicting epoch updates. assert convergence within X retries.

kevin: metrics we need: per-manifest apply latency, fraction partial, retry count, RPC delta vs broadcast baseline. also per-prefix failure reasons (ownership-mismatch, cas-failure, io-error).

anita: ops-playbook requests: what do we do if a hot tenant triggers a massive manifest and causes eviction storm?

maria: recommendations: limit manifest size (e.g., 500 prefixes), rate-limit manifests per cluster, and auto-slowdown when manifest-failure-rate > threshold. add an emergency abort endpoint that flips manifest to aborted and emits a compensating manifest that pins prefixes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: note 
Applying manifests >1000 prefixes may spike RPC QPS; default cluster throttle: 150 manifests/hour, manifest-size cap 500.

sam: rollback is tricky. rather than strict rollback, prefer compensating manifests (pin back, rehydrate). full rollback only if state machine supports reverse ops.

kevin: read-after-write consistency: when epoch jumps, readpath consults pending_manifest_set for a prefix and prefers local remap or falls back to consult owner node before returning cached value. cheap check to reduce staleness window.

maria: agreed. also plan to surface a "manifest-pending" tag on metrics so product teams can correlate errors to recent manifests.

ryan: i'll own chaos harness. sam/kevin want to pair on tests?

kevin: i'm in.

sam: free later today.

anita: i'll draft the ops playbook and UI wire for the manifest dashboard.

maria: thanks all. i'll iterate and then open RFC after the staging prototype. :thumbsup:
